disposition_reason: Selenium intake, excretion, absorption and whole-body selenium in four New Zealand women.

study.design: human metabolic study with stable selenium balance and radioactive selenium-75 tracers (selenomethionine and selenite)
study.method: fluorimetric stable selenium; gamma counting of selenium-75 in plasma, urine, feces and whole body

material.label_as_printed: Dietary selenium intake, ad libitum diet

findings.group: Four young New Zealand women, 14-day period
findings.notes: Balance +0.3 ug/d; urinary 13.1 and fecal 10.8 ug/d.
Calculated body pool, not a concentration.

regulatory_or_exposure: Abstract: mean dietary selenium 24.2 ug/d, urinary 13.1 ug/d, fecal 10.8 ug/d, balance +0.3 ug/d
Abstract: intestinal absorption of food selenium 0.76 to 0.83 of intake (mean 0.79)
Abstract: authors infer minimum dietary requirement probably not more than 20 ug/d
non_numeric_findings: Whole-body selenium estimates were lower when derived from selenite tracer (mean 2.6 to 3.5 mg) than from selenomethionine (mean 5.2 to 6.9 mg) (Abstract).
New Zealand topsoils 0.1 to 4.0 ug/g selenium; much South Island arable land below 0.5 ug/g (Introduction, citing earlier work).
